newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 30.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Monday:
- Irish police are investigating the murder of a man shot in a bookmakers.
- A report recommending pay rises for top earners in the public service will be the first test of the new government's mettle.
- Deputies to the EU assembly have rejected a move which would have obliged them to produce airline tickets, hotel and other receipts when claiming expenses.
- Hong Kong will revert to China at midnight, ending 156 years of British control.
- World heavyweight boxing champion Evander Hollyfield was in phlegmatic mood last night nursing a right ear, the top of which Mike Tyson had bitten of.

- Former transport minister Michael Lowry will dispute claims that he intervened with a Fine Gael councillor and member of parliament over tax designation status for a development site involving Dunnes Stores.
- Police have begun a murder investigation after a man was shot dead in a bookmakers on Saturday afternoon.
- Dole fraudsters are to come under further pressure after the government pledged to crack down on the black economy.
- Prime Minister Bertie Ahern is expected to fill holes in the map left by his decision to leave large sections of the country absent from the cabinet table.
- Top lawyers for former Prime Minsiter Charles Haughey will launch a full-scale effort on Monday to stop evidence being heard by the parments-to-politicians tribunal.
